options: A prompt with its fixed structure separated from named variables that change per call
A prompt written in a foreign language for translation practice
A system setting that limits how many tokens a model can output
A log of every prompt a user has ever sent
questions.explain: A template keeps the tested structure (role, format, constraints) fixed while only named variables change from one call to the next.

questions.q: In the customer-email template example, which of these is one of the template's variables?
options: {{customer_message}}
The word "Apologize"
The instruction to keep the reply under a word limit
The phrase "Write a reply to this customer email"
questions.explain: {{customer_message}}, along with {{resolution_options}} and {{max_words}}, is one of the parts pulled out as a variable; the surrounding instructions stay fixed.

questions.q: Why does filling the same template with two different sets of values still produce consistent results?
options: Because the fixed structure — tone, format, rules — stays identical across both fills
Because the model ignores the variables and always gives the same answer
Because both fills happen to use the exact same customer message
Because templates only work when the variables are identical
questions.explain: The template's fixed, tested structure stays the same regardless of which values fill the variables, which is what keeps the output consistent.

questions.q: What makes a template variable "too broad," according to this lesson?
options: It only ever holds a single word
It tries to hold an entire instruction inside it, effectively becoming a new prompt each time
It is given a long, descriptive variable name
It is reused across more than one template
questions.explain: A variable like {{instructions}} that gets filled with a full paragraph of new rules each call defeats templating — you're hand-writing a prompt again, just with extra steps.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what should stay in the template itself rather than become a variable?
options: The role, tone, format, and constraints that should apply on every call
The customer's actual message text
A specific order number
The maximum word count for this particular request
questions.explain: The fixed, tested parts of the prompt — role, tone, format, and constraints — belong in the template structure itself, not in a variable.
